newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt sinks, U.S. rate hike fears loom.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt sinks, U.S. rate hike fears loom.

text.p: Emerging debt prices sank as recent fears of a possible hike in U.S. interest rates continued to spook the market, analysts and traders said.

"The correction that a majority of participants have been expecting, and fearing for some time has happened - the bubble has burst," said Richard Siegal, Head of Fixed Income at Santander Investments.
Concerns that the second leg of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, on Wednesday, might prompt more hawkish comments continued to depress prices, players said.
Last week, inflation warnings by Greenspan during his testimony sparked a selloff in the U.S. Treasury and stock markets as fears of a possible rate hike gripped the markets.
"Greenspan has cited repeated concerns about the stock market," said Siegal. "He's also cited, specifically, that there's a real risk that interest rates may have to rise."

"The concern is not so much that rates will go up...the "big fear" is how long the tightening by the Fed will last," Siegal added. "If inflation fails to come under control, or if the Fed sees that inflation has longer legs then it wants, then the tightening could last for a year or more."
Among Monday's key losers were Russian VN US$ bonds which sank 3-1/8 points to trade at 80-1/4 bid. Bulgaria IAB debt also suffered a 2-3/8 point loss to trade at a 57-5/8 bid.
Venez Pars traded off 2-3/4 to 74-1/8 bid while Brazil C bonds dropped 1-7/8 to trade at a 77-1/8 bid.

"Our market has been overpriced for a while," said one trader. "For the the last two months or so, there's been no offered paper at all...paper just continued to tighten and tighten, and customers and dealers became a bit complacent."

"Greenspan's speech has made people nervous," the trader added. "We saw some institutional selling, then more by those holding defensive positions...right now the market's trying to swallow up some inventory."
Among other Brady issues, Argentina Pars fell 1-1/8 to a 65-1/4 bid, Discounts also lossed two points to trade at an 81 bid, while FRBs were off 1-1/8 to trade at an 89 bid.
Mexico Pars lossed 1-1/8 to trade at a 75 bid and Discount were off 7/8 at 90-3/8 bid.
"Some bonds have cheapend to the point where they probably look reasonably attractive," said another trader.

"From a momentum play you'll probably see the market go a little bit lower in the short-term, especially given Friday's (U.S.) employment numbers," he added. "The Street's mostly expecting the numbers to come in on the high side."
On Friday, the U.S. Labor Department is scheduled to release February unemployment and nonfarm paryolls.

In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists predict the rate of unemployment will ease to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent in January. Nonfarm payrolls are expected to increase by 230,00 compared to a gain of 271,00 in January.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond was off 12/32 at 97-11/32 to yield 6.83 percent, at the close.
